exactclaim: The \mappe{} studies relating prediction-side quantities to explanation change agree the link is weak.
evidence_location: N616 local primary PDF pp20–21; S52§5.2; S75§6
evidence_summary: Studies concern different targets; S77 links OOS uncertainty and instability, and S52 reports a strong association.
safest_replacement: Prediction accuracy or robustness alone does not guarantee explanation stability; the relationship depends on the measured prediction quantity, explanation target and perturbation regime.

exactclaim: quantised models kept their ROC-AUC while SHAP rankings changed
evidence_location: Publisher article shell; no substantive paper text retrieved
evidence_summary: Exact DOI/title identified; primary abstract/results inaccessible in tool.
safest_replacement: Drop this example until the primary results can be inspected; do not infer unchanged AUC from metadata.

exactclaim: better accuracy did not bring more reliable explanations
evidence_summary: LR has most stable retraining explanations but weaker detection; reliability components differ.
safest_replacement: Across two intrusion datasets, the most accurate models did not have the most reproducible SHAP profiles; reliability also depended on the diagnostic.

exactclaim: better accuracy did not bring more reliable explanations
evidence_location: Primary local N383 abstract;Methods explanation metrics;Discussion
evidence_summary: Finer DEM predictive gains do not synchronously improve stability/domain consistency.
safest_replacement: In this landslide case study, finer DEMs improved prediction without consistently improving SHAP stability or geomorphic consistency.

exactclaim: Under attack, prediction robustness and explanation stability were distinct axes
evidence_summary: RI and ESI can decouple; estimates use distinct held-out subsets and fixed-seed single runs.
safest_replacement: Under the evaluated attacks, prediction robustness and SHAP stability could diverge; these fixed-seed estimates were obtained on separate held-out subsets.

exactclaim: XGBoost's piecewise-constant surface defeats gradient-free attacks yet leaves explanations unstable
evidence_summary: ZOO approximates gradients; Square Attack reveals vulnerability.
safest_replacement: XGBoost’s piecewise-constant surface made finite-difference ZOO ineffective within leaves, while Square Attack exposed prediction vulnerability and attribution drift remained measurable.

exactclaim: the closest, Tolay \cite{S62}, uses TreeSHAP only and is a preprint
evidence_summary: TreeSHAP stability tested for tree models; LR is a predictive baseline; no LIME stability experiment.
safest_replacement: Tolay’s arXiv study evaluates TreeSHAP stability for tree models rather than a joint SHAP–LIME stability comparison.

evidence_summary: Accepts same predicted class and confidence change no greater than0.05.
safest_replacement: S62 retains bounded traffic-feature perturbations only when the predicted class is unchanged and attack-confidence change is at most0.05.

exactclaim: prediction-equivalent models from different hypothesis classes gave different attributions
evidence_summary: Same explanation method across different model classes; not a within-model local perturbation test.
safest_replacement: Prediction-equivalent models from different hypothesis classes can assign different SHAP attributions; this is cross-model disagreement.

exactclaim: a tree-structure score tracked disagreement between prediction-equivalent models
evidence_summary: R(x) averages pairwise attribution-rank correlations over a reference ensemble; paper acknowledges single-model implementation gap.
safest_replacement: A multi-model attribution-agreement score assessed cross-architecture explanation reliability; it requires an existing reference ensemble and is not computed from tree structure alone.

evidence_summary: No input perturbation needed for R, but multiple models and their explanations required.
safest_replacement: Classify S75 as a multi-model agreement diagnostic, not a cheap model-alone predictor; revise corresponding evidence-map counts.

exactclaim: instability was lower where forecast uncertainty was low
evidence_summary: Low-uncertainty separation holds for OOS metrics; IS instability can invert for Wave-like sigmoid/piecewise models.
safest_replacement: In synthetic experiments, out-of-sample instability was lower in low-uncertainty regions; ordinary in-sample instability sometimes showed the opposite ordering.

exactclaim: gradient-boosted trees show the same instability near segment boundaries as smooth non-linear models
evidence_summary: Boundary-crossing local linear instability and forecast uncertainty are studied using synthetic generators.
safest_replacement: The study links segment-boundary crossings to local explanatory instability in simulated piecewise models, alongside instability in smooth nonlinear models; it distinguishes OOS and IS measures.

exactclaim: 68\% of77 datasets showed SHAP instability, with rankings of correlated pairs close to a coin flip
evidence_location: §10.16 survey methodology and selection caveat; symmetry theory
evidence_summary: 52/77 benchmark datasets cross ranking-flip threshold across20XGBoost refits; coin-flip limit concerns symmetric/nearly symmetric pairs.
safest_replacement: In one77-dataset benchmark survey,52 datasets exceeded a10%global SHAP ranking-flip threshold across20XGBoost refits; symmetric correlated pairs can approach chance ordering.

exactclaim: a split-count screen flagged ranking instability across retrained models
evidence_summary: Per-tree split-frequency screen proxies global feature-pair rank flips; assumptions/calibration constrain transfer.
safest_replacement: A single-model split-frequency screen flagged feature pairs prone to global ranking reversals across refits, under stated assumptions and empirical calibration.

exactclaim: This narrower gap allows existing diagnostics of retraining instability
evidence_summary: Global retraining diagnostic is not a local input-perturbation fragility detector.
safest_replacement: Retain; explicitly distinguish global feature-pair retraining diagnostics from instance-level prediction-preserving input perturbation.

exactclaim: epistemic uncertainty correlated strongly and negatively with stability
evidence_summary: XD is Kendall agreement despite degradation name; negative XEC means increasing uncertainty accompanies declining agreement.
safest_replacement: Across perturbation strengths, epistemic growth was generally negatively associated with Kendall attribution agreement, with weaker settings; the direction is uncertainty up, stability down.

evidence_summary: Gating avoids attribution perturbations at inference, but uncertainty uses ensemble/dropout/bootstrap or RF surrogate and validation perturbs inputs.
safest_replacement: Uncertainty can guide explanation gating without generating perturbed explanations at inference; its estimation and validation still have model/ensemble and perturbation costs.

evidence_summary: Conformal uncertainty uses held-out labeled residuals and neighborhood quantiles without query perturbations or refitting the base model. Local-linear uncertainty fits a local surrogate. Instability targets themselves require perturbations. Neither is tree structure alone.
safest_replacement: Conformal uncertainty can serve as a gate using held-out calibration outcomes without perturbing the query; local-surrogate and instability calculations have additional costs. Distinguish this from a score computed only from one fitted tree model.
